business_summary: An apparel brand selling comfort socks and tees with a buy-one-give-one model that donates an item to individuals experiencing homelessness for every purchase made.
stated_claims: Every purchase donates an item to someone experiencing homelessness

relevant_tags.why: The brand explicitly sells comfort socks as a core product.
Socks and tees are core everyday basic apparel items.
Socks and tees are clothing items that fall directly under apparel.
The advertiser notes that their products are great for gifting.

note_signals.why: Heartfoot sells socks and basics, and notes that its audience responds strongly to social-good messaging and gifting, which perfectly matches this advertiser.
Kitchenly targets family households, which aligns with the advertiser's focus on families buying multi-packs.

gate_reason: The product offerings (socks and tees), social-good mission, target audiences (families and gifters), and average order value ($65) are clearly stated and easy to align with publishers.
clarifying_questions: What is the starting retail price for a single pair of socks and a single tee?
Are your products made from organic or sustainable materials?
Do you offer any subscription options for your multi-packs?
